chapters.name: Prologue — The Breadboard and the Centroid
story: The breadboard is the physical carrier. Row 1 is the +5V rail, row 2 the collector taps, row 5 the bases, row 10 the emitters, rows 15/20 the LED anodes and cathodes.
Every operation reduces to XOR. Four faces realize the four phases: BOOT0 (bind, 5T), BOOT1 (apply, 6T), SECURE (eval, 8T), USER (digest, 10T).
principles: The carrier is the transport. The graph is the structure.
Rails: +5V, GND, DATA BUS make every subgraph shareable.

cues.text: Lay the rails: +5V row 1, GND row 20, DATA BUS across.
The centroid gate: BOOT0 ^ BOOT1 ^ SECURE ^ USER.

chapters.name: XOR #1 — Bind (5T)
story: XOR #1 is a NAND gate on the left two transistors, a switch for the middle transistor, and an OR-like gate for the last two.
It can only show its result: current flows into the circuit and through the LED. It has no fan-out — BOOT0 is a terminal.
principles: The bind phase constructs the relation; it cannot drive downstream.

build.text: C(Q2) → B(Q3) [NAND output drives switch base]

cues.text: Bind: A → 2K → B(Q1), B → 2K → B(Q2).
NAND wire-AND: E(Q2) → C(Q1). Switch drives Q3.
OR-like: Q3 drives Q4 and Q5; E(Q4) → C(Q5).
Output: C(Q4) → 330Ω → RED LED. BOOT0 = bind output.

chapters.name: XOR #2 — Apply (6T)
story: XOR #2 is XOR #1 plus one transistor on the right-hand side — Q6, acting as an inverter.
The LED direction is flipped and current flows OUT of the circuit. The output can be sent elsewhere — BOOT1 is a source, so it can drive the eval stage.
principles: The apply phase needs fan-out. One inverter transistor turns a terminal into a source.
BOOT1 = BOOT0 inverted through the Q6 inverter stage.

build.text: C(Q6) → 330Ω → YELLOW LED. BOOT1 = apply output.

cues.text: Apply: C(Q4) → 2K → B(Q6) inverter stage.
C(Q6) → 330Ω → YELLOW LED. BOOT1 = apply output.

chapters.name: XOR #3 — Eval (8T)
story: XOR #3 is built from 4 NAND gates, each requiring 2 transistors: 8 transistors total.
NAND1 = ~(A & B); NAND2 = ~(A & NAND1); NAND3 = ~(B & NAND1); NAND4 = ~(NAND2 & NAND3).
The 4-NAND structure is gate-level composable. SECURE stores receipts and each receipt must be independently addressable — the composable topology gives that.
principles: Eval is composed of identical subgates.
SECURE must be composable to keep receipts independently verifiable.

build.text: NAND1 wire-AND: E(Q8) → C(Q7); NAND1 = C(Q8)
NAND2 wire-AND: E(Q10) → C(Q9); NAND2 = C(Q10)
B → Q11; NAND1 → B(Q12); NAND3 = C(Q12)
NAND4 wire-AND: E(Q14) → C(Q13); NAND4 = C(Q14)

cues.text: Eval: NAND1 = ~(A & B) built from Q7, Q8.
NAND2 = ~(A & NAND1); NAND3 = ~(B & NAND1).
NAND4 = ~(NAND2 & NAND3).
Output: C(Q14) → 330Ω → GREEN LED. SECURE = eval output.

chapters.name: XOR #4 — Digest (10T)
story: XOR #4 is built from 5 NOR gates, each requiring 2 transistors: 10 transistors total.
NOR1 = ~(A | B); NOR2 = ~(A | NOR1); NOR3 = ~(B | NOR1); NOR4 = ~(NOR2 | NOR3); NOR5 buffers NOR4.
The 5-NOR topology is the most reliable — precedent: the Apollo Guidance Computer ran on NOR gates because NOR was the most trusted topology.
principles: Digest maximizes reliability — NOR-only mirrors the Apollo Guidance Computer.
USER is where the data lives; it must be the most robust face.

build.text: B → Q19; NOR1 → B(Q20); NOR3 collectors tied

cues.text: Digest: NOR1 = ~(A | B) built from Q15, Q16.
NOR2 = ~(A | NOR1); NOR3 = ~(B | NOR1).
NOR4 = ~(NOR2 | NOR3).
NOR5 buffers NOR4 → BLUE LED. USER = digest output.

chapters.name: Epilogue — The Centroid and the Meta-Compile
story: The tetrahedral centroid is the XOR of the four faces: Centroid = BOOT0 ^ BOOT1 ^ SECURE ^ USER.
The transistor count increases monotonically 5 → 6 → 8 → 10 because each face adds capability: BOOT0 constructs, BOOT1 drives, SECURE composes, USER carries.
When the walkthrough is complete, the meta-compilation is complete: every canvas node traces back to its physical realization, every vertex and every edge is one line of the JSONL/NDJSON stream.

cues.text: Wire the centroid gate: BOOT0 ^ BOOT1 ^ SECURE ^ USER.
Green centroid LED illuminates at the terminal. Meta-compilation complete.
